subject: Literature
title: Greek Tragedy and the Origins of Drama
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Greek Tragedy and the Origins of Drama.

hook.text: All of Western theatre began with one man stepping out of a chorus and speaking as an individual character.

buildup.text: Thespis invented acting around 534 BC, and Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides perfected tragic drama.

discovery.text: Greek tragedies used mythology to explore justice, fate, and the limits of human knowledge before audiences.

twist.text: Of the thousands of tragedies performed, only thirty-three complete plays survive from just three playwrights.

climax.text: Greek tragedy invented drama as a communal experience where a city watched its own values tested on stage.

punchline.text: One man leaving a chorus invented all of theatre.

quiz.question: How many complete Greek tragedies survive today?
